es: Abrir una conversación, crear afinidad, cerrarla y redactar un mensaje de seguimiento cordial con recordatorio, detalle, propuesta concreta, salida fácil y despedida.

usesVocabulary: pick up where we left off

vocabulary.es: ponerse al día, retomar el contacto

vocabulary.en: pick up where we left off

teaching.en: A vague message like 'Let's keep in touch' rarely leads to a second meeting, because it leaves the other person to work out what you actually want.
teaching.es: Un mensaje vago como «Mantengámonos en contacto» rara vez lleva a un segundo encuentro, porque deja al otro la tarea de adivinar qué quieres realmente.
teaching.explanationEs: Vague es lo contrario de concrete: sin día, hora ni plan.
segments: A vague message like 'Let's keep in touch' rarely leads to a second meeting,
because it leaves the other person to work out what you actually want.
teaching.audioText: A vague message like 'Let's keep in touch' rarely leads to a second meeting, because it leaves the other person to work out what you actually want.

teaching.en: Remind the person who you are and why you reach out, perhaps naming a mutual acquaintance: 'We met at the wedding, by the cake table.'
teaching.es: Recuerda a la persona quién eres y por qué le escribes, quizá nombrando a un conocido en común: «Nos conocimos en la boda, junto a la mesa de los postres».
teaching.explanationEs: Reach out es contactar con alguien; remind + persona + dato que lo ubique.
segments: Remind the person who you are and why you reach out, perhaps naming
a mutual acquaintance: 'We met at the wedding, by the cake table.'
teaching.audioText: Remind the person who you are and why you reach out, perhaps naming a mutual acquaintance: 'We met at the wedding, by the cake table.'

teaching.en: A quick recap of one detail shows that you listened, and it lets you touch base without sounding like a salesman or a stranger.
teaching.es: Un breve resumen de un detalle demuestra que escuchaste, y te permite retomar el contacto sin sonar como un vendedor ni como un extraño.
teaching.explanationEs: Recap: menciona algo que dijo («You said you were training for a marathon»).
segments: A quick recap of one detail shows that you listened, and it
lets you touch base without sounding like a salesman or a stranger.
teaching.audioText: A quick recap of one detail shows that you listened, and it lets you touch base without sounding like a salesman or a stranger.

teaching.en: Then propose something concrete: 'Would you like to have coffee next Thursday at ten, so that we can pick up where we left off?'
teaching.es: Después propón algo concreto: «¿Te apetece tomar un café el próximo jueves a las diez, para que retomemos donde lo dejamos?».
teaching.explanationEs: Concrete = día, hora y plan; en inglés se dice «have coffee», no «take a coffee».
segments: Then propose something concrete: 'Would you like to have coffee next Thursday
at ten, so that we can pick up where we left off?'
teaching.audioText: Then propose something concrete: 'Would you like to have coffee next Thursday at ten, so that we can pick up where we left off?'

teaching.en: When the other person suggests something, you can answer 'I'd love to take you up on that', and a gentle nudge a week later is perfectly acceptable.
teaching.es: Cuando la otra persona sugiere algo, puedes contestar «Me encantaría aceptar tu invitación», y un suave recordatorio una semana después es perfectamente aceptable.
teaching.explanationEs: Take you up on = aceptar una oferta; nudge es un recordatorio educado, nunca una presión.
segments: When the other person suggests something, you can answer 'I'd love to take you
up on that', and a gentle nudge a week later is perfectly acceptable.
teaching.audioText: When the other person suggests something, you can answer 'I'd love to take you up on that', and a gentle nudge a week later is perfectly acceptable.

teaching.en: End with a low-pressure sign-off such as 'Warm regards', and remind the other person that saying no is fine: 'No worries if you are busy.'
teaching.es: Termina con una despedida sin presión, como «Un saludo cordial», y recuerda al otro que puede decir que no: «No pasa nada si estás ocupado».
teaching.explanationEs: El sign-off cierra el mensaje; la salida fácil quita presión y hace más probable un sí.
segments: End with a low-pressure sign-off such as 'Warm regards', and remind the other
person that saying no is fine: 'No worries if you are busy.'

prompt.es: Elige el mensaje que combina recordatorio, detalle y propuesta concreta.

choices.text: Hi Tom, it was lovely to meet you at the book fair. Let's keep in touch, and perhaps we can meet some time when we are both free to do so.
Hi Tom, I am writing to formally request a meeting at your earliest convenience concerning volunteers for your theatre group.
Hi Tom, we met at the book fair by the coffee stand. You mentioned your theatre group needs volunteers, so could we meet on Friday at five?

feedback.es: Solo el primer mensaje sitúa dónde se conocieron, retoma el detalle de los voluntarios y propone día y hora; los otros son vagos o demasiado rígidos.

hint.es: Busca día, hora y un detalle de la charla.

origin.text: Mia wants to write to a man she met at a book fair. He had said that his small theatre group needs volunteers for the autumn show.

prompt.es: Completa: «Te escribo para ponerme en contacto tras nuestra charla en la boda.»

feedback.es: Reach out significa ponerse en contacto con alguien, y es el verbo habitual para abrir un mensaje de seguimiento.

hint.es: Es el verbo que acompaña a «out» para contactar.

origin.text: It was lovely to meet you at the wedding on Saturday. I am writing to ___ out after our chat, because I would love to continue the conversation over coffee.

prompt.es: Ordena: «¿Te apetece tomar un café el próximo jueves a las diez?»

answer.text: Would you like to have coffee next Thursday at ten

feedback.es: La propuesta concreta usa «Would you like to» y da el día y la hora.

hint.es: Empieza con la fórmula de invitación.

prompt.es: Escucha el mensaje de voz y elige qué propone Tom y cómo deja una salida fácil.

choices.text: A first guitar lesson on Saturday, with another date if needed.
A guitar concert on Saturday, with a refund if you need it.
A weekly class from next month, with no other option.

feedback.es: Tom propone una primera clase el sábado a las once y ofrece otra fecha si no le conviene: propuesta concreta más salida fácil.

origin.audio: Hi Ana, it's Tom, from the wedding, the one who dropped a glass of juice beside the cake table. You mentioned that you were looking for a teacher for your cousin's guitar lessons, and I happen to give lessons on Saturdays. Would you like to try a first session with her this Saturday at eleven? There is no pressure, of course, and if the date does not suit you, just tell me and we will find another one.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase del mensaje con la función que cumple.

pairs: I'm the one who lost an umbrella at the fair.
You said the trains to Cuenca are always late.
Shall we meet on Friday at noon?
No pressure if the week is full.

feedback.es: Cada frase cumple una función distinta: identificarte, demostrar atención, proponer un plan y quitar presión.

pairs: I'm the one who lost an umbrella at the fair.
You said the trains to Cuenca are always late.
Shall we meet on Friday at noon?
No pressure if the week is full.

prompt.es: Lee el borrador y elige su problema principal.

choices.text: It is too formal for a message between two guests.
It is too vague to lead to a second meeting.
It is too long to be read in a single go.

feedback.es: No da día, lugar ni detalle de la charla: «some time» y «call me maybe» dejan al otro sin nada que responder.

origin.text: 'Hey! Loved the party. We should meet up some time, call me maybe. Bye!' Mia sent this to a man she had talked to for an hour, and she never received an answer.

prompt.es: Lee el correo de Mia y elige qué pretende con su doble oferta.

choices.text: To test how keen Leo really is about his marathon training.
To avoid having to name a day for the meeting herself.
To make replying easy by offering two light options.

feedback.es: Ofrecer enviar el artículo o tomar un café baja el esfuerzo de responder; además Mia sí concreta día y hora, y cierra con «No worries».

origin.text: Hi Leo, it's Mia from Ana and Tom's wedding. You said you were training for a marathon, so I thought you might like the article I mentioned. Shall I send it by email, or would you prefer to have coffee next Thursday at ten, and I can bring a printed copy? No worries either way.

prompt.es: Escucha el mensaje de voz y elige por qué será difícil responder.

choices.text: It gives no day, place or plan that he can accept.
It is so formal that he will not feel able to answer.
It asks for a reply so soon that he has no time.

feedback.es: Todo son «some time», «maybe» y «at some point»: sin propuesta concreta, el oyente no tiene nada a lo que contestar.

origin.audio: Hi, it's Sara, from the book fair. It was really nice to meet you. We should get together some time, maybe, whenever you are free. Anyway, let's keep in touch, and I'll be in touch at some point. Take care.

prompt.es: Completa: «Me encantaría aceptar tu invitación a ese café la semana que viene.»

feedback.es: Take you up on es aceptar una oferta o invitación que otro ha hecho, y es más natural que «accept your invitation».

origin.text: Thank you for a lovely evening, and for mentioning that little café near the station. I'd love to ___ you up on that coffee next week, as long as Thursday still works.

prompt.es: Redacta el mensaje de seguimiento a Leo con recordatorio, detalle, propuesta y despedida.

answer.text: Hi Leo, it's Mia from Ana and Tom's wedding. We met by the cake table, and I hope you don't mind me getting in touch. I have been thinking about our chat ever since. You said you were training for a marathon and that you were looking for someone to run with in the mornings, so I wanted to reach out. I have also found the article about training that I mentioned, and I would be happy to send it to you. Would you like to have coffee next Thursday at ten, at the café in the square? We could pick up where we left off and talk about the route. No worries at all if you are busy, and feel free to suggest another day. Either way, it was great chatting with you. Warm regards, Mia
accepted: Hi Leo, it's Mia from Ana and Tom's wedding. We met by the cake table, and I hope you don't mind me getting in touch. I have been thinking about our chat ever since. You said you were training for a marathon and that you were looking for someone to run with in the mornings, so I wanted to reach out. I have also found the article about training that I mentioned, and I would be happy to send it to you. Would you like to have coffee next Thursday at ten, at the café in the square? We could pick up where we left off and talk about the route. No worries at all if you are busy, and feel free to suggest another day. Either way, it was great chatting with you. Warm regards, Mia

Hello Leo, this is Mia, and we met at the wedding of Ana and Tom, by the cake table. I really enjoyed our chat about your marathon training, and I remembered that you want a partner for your morning runs. I have found the article about training that I promised you, so I can send it to you whenever you like. Would you like to have coffee next Thursday at 10 in the café on the square? That way we could pick up where we left off and plan a first run together. No problem at all if the week is too busy for you, we can easily find another day. Thank you again for the lovely conversation. Best wishes, Mia

feedback.es: El mensaje recuerda el lugar, retoma el maratón y las carreras matinales, cumple la promesa del artículo, propone día y hora concretos y deja una salida fácil con una despedida cordial.

origin.text: Datos: conociste a Leo en la boda de Ana y Tom, junto a la mesa de los postres. Entrena para un maratón y busca compañía para correr por las mañanas; le prometiste enviarle un artículo sobre entrenamiento. Propón un café el próximo jueves a las 10 en el café de la plaza, deja una salida fácil y despídete con calidez.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige con qué fin habla Leo de un «gentle nudge».

choices.text: To cancel the coffee plans and blame the busy week.
To remind her politely and leave the choice to her.
To insist that she must decide by Thursday at the latest.

feedback.es: Un nudge es un recordatorio suave: Leo retoma el plan, dice «no pressure» y ofrece otra fecha, sin cancelar ni exigir.

origin.audio: Hi Mia, Leo here. Just a gentle nudge about the coffee we mentioned. I know the week has been busy, so no pressure at all. If Thursday is still too soon, I am free on Saturday morning, and I can meet you at any place that suits you best.

prompt.es: Lee el borrador y elige la despedida que mejor encaja con su registro.

choices.text: Cheers, see you around!
Yours faithfully, Miss Mia
Kind regards, Mia

feedback.es: El mensaje es cordial y semiformal: «Kind regards» encaja; «Cheers» es demasiado informal y «Yours faithfully» demasiado rígido para alguien a quien ya conoces.

origin.text: Dear Dr Sol, it was lovely to meet you at the conference. I enjoyed our conversation about rural clinics and would love to hear more. Would you be free for a short call next week? If not, I completely understand. ___

prompt.es: Completa: «Conviene retomar la charla donde la dejamos: menciona primero el maratón.»

feedback.es: Pick up where we left off es retomar la conversación en el punto donde se interrumpió, que es lo que hace un buen seguimiento.

origin.text: You don't have to start from nothing in your message. It is better to pick ___ where you left off: mention the marathon first and then make your proposal.
